commits.edited_message:
mprintf: avoid scanning strings twice for unbounded %s

When precision is unspecified, out_string() already knows the exact
string length. Pass it directly to stream_run() instead of scanning
again in stream_zrun().

A literal negative precision is defined to be omitted too, but unlike
the '*' form it arrives still negative. Confirm the terminator when
the alternate form quotes the value and, when that stays on the
terminator, use the same single-pass copy.

Keep the bounded, NUL-aware scan for explicit precision, including
non-NUL-terminated buffers. Document why the two paths differ.

Closes #23019

mprintf: use size_t width for the bare Windows %I modifier

The bare "%I" length modifier (without an explicit "32" or "64"
suffix) is Microsoft's non-standard way to size an integer conversion
to the platform's native pointer/size_t width: 4 bytes on 32-bit
Windows, 8 bytes on 64-bit Windows. parse_flags() instead based the
choice on SIZEOF_CURL_OFF_T, which is 8 on both, so on 32-bit Windows
a bare "%In"/"%Id"/"%Iu" was always treated as 8-byte wide. For "%n"
this made the MTYPE_INTPTR sink write an 8-byte int64_t through a
caller-supplied pointer to a 4-byte destination, corrupting adjacent
memory; for "%Id"/"%Iu" it fetched 8 bytes from the argument list
where the caller passed a 4-byte value.

Switch the bare "%I" case to SIZEOF_SIZE_T, matching the same pattern
already used for "%z". Explicit "%I32"/"%I64" are unaffected. curl's
own code does not use the bare "%I" modifier anywhere.

Added test 1451 for verification (Windows-only).

The omitted-precision terminator check now covers the left-align flag
as well as the alternate form.

Reported-by: Joshua Rogers
Closes #23030

mprintf: make mprintf() and mfprintf() return -1 on error

Previously they returned the number of characters it output at the time
of the error, but that is not only contrary to what POSIX does, it also
makes it next to impossible for a caller to know when for example the
output failed because out of disk space or similar.

The omitted-precision terminator check now covers an explicit field
width too.

Verified by test 2380
Closes #23112

coupling: out_string() folds a literal negative precision (POSIX: precision omitted) only after a shared cursor, initialized to strlen(str), has confirmed the terminator. Each edited commit adds one modifier to that cursor: alternate form ('#'), left-align ('-'), then an explicit field width. Every modifier loads str[off] and then increments off. One modifier therefore reads the terminating NUL, which is inside the caller's object, leaves prec folded to omitted, and matches documented output. A second modifier loads the following byte, one past the object. The PoC passes all three flags at once (%#-2.-2s), so deleting or reverting any single commit's added load still leaves the other two sharing the cursor and the second load still runs off the end. No individual diff is an out-of-bounds read on its own: the first commit's only load is at strlen, and each later diff adds one load at the cursor the earlier modifier already advanced.
